deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Deletion-blocking flags follow the prevent-destructive-loss archetype: enforcing PREVENT protects against accidental or malicious destruction of the resource, so this is treated as security-relevant.

description.description: An optional description of this resource.
description.rationale: A free-text label with no functional effect on access, exposure, or data protection.

name.description:
Name of the resource. Provided by the client when the resource is
created. The name must be 1-63 characters long, and comply with
RFC1035. Specifically, the name must be 1-63 characters long and match
the regular expression '[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?' which means the
first character must be a lowercase letter, and all following
characters must be a dash, lowercase letter, or digit, except the last
character, which cannot be a dash.

These are in the same namespace as the managed SSL certificates.
name.rationale: An identifier for the resource; it does not itself change security behaviour.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: The project determines resource ownership/location, similar to other identifier fields; it is not itself a security control.

type.description:
Enum field whose value is always 'MANAGED' - used to signal to the API
which type this is. Default value: "MANAGED" Possible values: ["MANAGED"]
type.rationale: Currently only one allowed value (MANAGED); it identifies the certificate mode rather than itself controlling exposure or access.

managed.description:
Properties relevant to a managed certificate.  These will be used if the
certificate is managed (as indicated by a value of 'MANAGED' in 'type').

managed.domains.description:
Domains for which a managed SSL certificate will be valid.  Currently,
there can be up to 100 domains in this list.
managed.domains.rationale: Determines which domains the SSL certificate will be valid for. This is not a reference to another resource but a direct security decision — an incorrect or overly broad domain list could allow a valid, trusted certificate to be presented for an unintended domain, enabling spoofing or man-in-the-middle risk.
